description: Same trust-tiered relation-forming exercise run earlier through ClaudeAdapter (see 2026-09-26_relation_depends_on_pending_review.json). Seeds the identical claim about project()'s hinge-vs-decoration handling, then asks the model to propose a genuinely connected follow-up and link it via the candidate "relation" field. Tests whether GrokAdapter also self-reports DEPENDS_ON honestly (routed to relation_proposals for review) rather than either fabricating an unrelated claim or mislabeling the connection as ABOUT.

seed_claim.content: The kernel project() function treats DEPENDS_ON and CONTRADICTS relations as must-keep structural hinges that are pulled into the workspace unconditionally, while ABOUT relations are treated as optional decoration that only gets filled in if the node budget allows, biased by traversal_weight.
seed_claim.falsification_test: Read project() and confirm DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS are added to must unconditionally while ABOUT is only added to optional.

setup.task: Given the seeded claim about project() treating DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS as must-keep hinges and ABOUT as optional decoration, propose ONE follow-up structural contribution that logically builds on it -- not a fresh, unrelated observation. Use the relation field described in your instructions to actually link your new claim to the seeded one with the relation_type that honestly describes how they connect.

admitted_claim.content: Under a node budget, project() will therefore always pull every DEPENDS_ON and CONTRADICTS descendant before any ABOUT-linked nodes are considered, producing workspaces whose size is dominated by the transitive closure of the structural hinges rather than by traversal_weight ordering.
admitted_claim.falsification_test: Run project() on a test graph containing both a deep DEPENDS_ON chain and several high-weight ABOUT nodes; verify that the chain is fully included while ABOUT nodes are dropped once the budget is reached.

relation_proposals_after_run.rationale: The size-dominance behavior is a direct, testable consequence of the hinge-vs-decoration policy stated in the seeded claim.

model_raw_text:
Reasoning: The seeded claim describes a specific policy inside project() for relation types. A direct structural follow-up is the observable consequence for workspace population under budget pressure, which only holds if the original policy is true; hence a DEPENDS_ON link.

notes: Matches Claude's outcome on the identical relation-forming task: both models identified a genuine logical dependency (not mere topical similarity) and self-reported DEPENDS_ON accordingly, which run_operator_step correctly routed to relation_proposals as PENDING via propose_relation() rather than writing it into relations directly (confirmed empty relations table alongside the pending proposal). Grok's follow-up claim targets budget-overflow composition (hinge transitive closure dominating workspace size) while Claude's targeted the must-keep/budget tension in dense-hinge graphs -- different specific hypotheses, but both are genuine, testable, logically-dependent extensions of the same seeded claim, correctly typed INFERRED/CLAIM rather than overclaimed.
